description: Open source AI clip generator: turns long videos into viral 9:16 shorts with AI moment detection, face tracking, subtitles and dubbing. Self-host free with Docker (MIT), or use the cloud with GPU speed from $12/mo. MCP server and API for AI agents.

summary.one_liner: OpenShorts is an open-source, self-hostable AI video tool that turns long videos into 9:16 shorts with moment detection, face-tracked cropping, subtitles and dubbing, plus AI UGC actor videos and YouTube title/thumbnail tools.
summary.what_it_does: The Clip Generator takes long-form video (podcasts, webinars, interviews) and detects 3-15 high-potential moments using an LLM (Google Gemini by default, or a local OpenAI-compatible server such as Ollama). It reframes each scene to 9:16 using modes such as face tracking (MediaPipe and YOLOv8), a blurred-background general mode, a split mode for two speakers, and a screencast mode. Word-level subtitles are generated with faster-whisper and burned in, with optional ElevenLabs dubbing, hook text overlays and Gemini-generated FFmpeg effects. A separate AI Shorts pipeline builds marketing videos with AI actors from a URL or description. The YouTube Studio tools generate titles, thumbnails and chapter descriptions and can publish to YouTube. Clips can be posted or scheduled to TikTok, Instagram and YouTube through the Upload-Post API, and the app exposes an API, an MCP endpoint, a CLI and an agent skill.
use_cases: turn a podcast or webinar into short clips
make TikTok, Reels or YouTube Shorts from long videos
self-host a free AI video clipper
generate UGC marketing videos with AI actors
create YouTube titles and thumbnails with AI
let an AI agent drive video clipping via MCP or API
how_to_run: pip install openshorts (or uvx openshorts) for the CLI
Self-hosted: clone the repo and run it with Docker (Docker Compose)
Set GEMINI_API_KEY in the client settings, or LLM_BASE_URL for a local model
Set AWS, LLM and concurrency variables in the server .env file if needed
Set OPENSHORTS_API_URL for self-hosted CLI use, or OPENSHORTS_API_KEY for hosted use
notable: Runs fully local with an OpenAI-compatible LLM server such as Ollama, LM Studio or vLLM, so no Google key is required
Layout is chosen per scene, including a split mode that stacks two speakers with captions on the seam
Ships a CLI, an MCP endpoint and an Agent Skills-format skill for AI agents
Bundles three tools in one app: clip generator, AI UGC actor videos and YouTube Studio
Client-side encrypted API keys, with no keys stored server-side
caveats: Self-hosting needs Docker, 8GB+ RAM and model downloads; the README says CPU processing takes 5 to 8 minutes per 8-minute video
Requires your own API keys (Gemini, ElevenLabs, fal.ai, Upload-Post) for many features
Hosted cloud has a watermark and 20 min/mo limit on the free plan; paid plans start at $12/mo
The cloud/ directory is under a separate source-available commercial license, not MIT
The self-hosted MCP endpoint only works while your machine is running
